set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule found. CalHFA perm term sheet (https://www.calhfa.ca.gov/multifamily/programs/forms/termsheet-perm-tax-exempt.pdf) and application and closing documents state no prevailing wage requirement. Federal: the loan is credit enhanced by HUD/FHA Risk Sharing, but 24 CFR 266.225(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/266.225) applies Davis-Bacon only when construction advances are insured, the work is new construction or substantial rehab, and there are 12 or more units; this is a permanent loan, so Risk Share alone does not trigger Davis-Bacon. State: CalHFA is a public lender, so coverage turns on Labor Code 1720(b)(4) below-market terms and 1720(c) exemptions for the specific deal.
set.audit_note: Prevailing wage left unclear: state outcome depends on Labor Code 1720(b)(4) and 1720(c) facts; Davis-Bacon not triggered by Risk Share on a perm-only loan per 24 CFR 266.225(a).

reason: No program rule or on-point ruling states prevailing wage for CalHFA permanent loans; Risk Share Davis-Bacon rule applies only to insured construction advances.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: DIR public works coverage determination PW 2004-016 (Rancho Santa Fe Village, CSCDA conduit bonds), as restated in DIR PW 2015-008 (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2015/2015-008.pdf): tax-exempt conduit revenue bond proceeds loaned to a developer through a bond trustee, where the issuer never holds the proceeds or repayments and bondholders look only to the developer and project, are not public funds under Labor Code 1720(b). CalHFA term sheets state no prevailing wage requirement. Condition: applies to the bond financing only; other public funds in the deal (soft loans, land write-downs, HOME, CDBG, or an elected CTCAC prevailing wage basis boost) can still trigger state prevailing wage or Davis-Bacon.

reason: DIR PW 2004-016 holds conduit tax-exempt bond proceeds are not public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), and the CalHFA conduit term sheet adds no prevailing wage requirement.
